title: Trade-In Agreements Mileage Deduction — Method of Calculation
content:
**Statement of method.** On a **Trade-In Agreements** agreement the mileage deduction is figured from the miles by which the inspected mileage exceeds the stated mileage: when that overage is greater than the grade's mileage tolerance, every mile of the overage is charged at the grade's mileage overage deduction per mile, and otherwise nothing is charged; the product is rounded to the nearest cent.

## Quantities

| Quantity | Where it is read |
|---|---|
| Stated mileage | The agreement: the odometer reading the customer stated when the offer was made |
| Inspected mileage | The agreement: the odometer reading recorded at the pickup inspection |
| Overage | The inspected mileage less the stated mileage |
| Mileage tolerance | The grade's figure for the agreement's condition grade |
| Rate per mile | The grade's mileage overage deduction per mile |

## Judgement

| Overage compared with the mileage tolerance | Miles charged | Deduction |
|---|---|---|
| Greater than the tolerance | Every mile of the overage, counted from the stated mileage | Overage multiplied by the rate per mile, rounded to the nearest cent |
| Equal to the tolerance | None | Nothing |
| Less than the tolerance | None | Nothing |

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

Hypothetical grade figures: a tolerance of 500 miles and a rate of $0.15 per mile.

- Stated mileage 42000, inspected mileage 43250: the overage is 1250 miles, greater than 500, so all 1250 miles are charged; 1250 multiplied by $0.15 is **$187.50**.
- Stated mileage 42000, inspected mileage 42500: the overage of 500 miles equals the tolerance, so nothing is charged.
- Stated mileage 42000, inspected mileage 42501: the overage of 501 miles is greater than 500; 501 multiplied by $0.15 is $75.15.
